h1: SEO Company in Chandigarh: two to eight real competitors, not a wall
metaTitle: SEO Company in Chandigarh: Win the Tricity Map Pack
metaDescription: Chandigarh's local pack is small enough to win with a proper Business Profile and real reviews. We cover the tricity on a 90-day baseline guarantee.
answer: Chandigarh is small — just over a million people at the 2011 census — and most commercial categories here have fewer than a dozen businesses doing serious SEO. That makes the local pack winnable with a properly built Google Business Profile and a steady flow of real reviews, often before you need a content retainer at all.
takeaways: Do the free work first. A complete Business Profile plus consistent real reviews beats a ₹75,000 retainer spent badly.
There's no published review threshold. The practical bar is **clearing the review count and rating of the current top three** in your category and area.
The tricity is three administrations — Chandigarh UT, Mohali in Punjab, Panchkula in Haryana. Google treats them as three places, and so should your pages.
Sector-level queries are real here in a way they aren't in most Indian cities. People genuinely search "dentist sector 35".
NRI property buyers research from Canada, the UK and Australia, which changes both the content and the hours your phone should be answered.

sections.h2: Count your actual competitors before you buy anything
body: Here's an exercise we'd rather you do before you talk to us, because it occasionally costs us the sale.

Open an incognito window, search your main service plus Chandigarh, and look past the map pack at the ten organic results. Count how many are local businesses with a real content library, a fast site and a visible review flow — rather than directories, aggregators and a five-page brochure site from 2019.

In most Chandigarh categories that count comes back between two and eight. In Delhi or Bangalore the same exercise returns a wall. That gap is the whole strategic argument for this city: the bar is low, so the work that clears it is small and cheap.
The corollary is uncomfortable for agencies. If the bar is that low, a lot of Chandigarh businesses do not need a retainer yet. They need about six weeks of setup and then discipline.

callout.title: What we say on the first call
callout.body: If your Business Profile is unclaimed, your site is slow and you have eleven reviews, we'll tell you to fix those three things before signing anything. It's not generosity — a retainer that starts before the basics are done spends its first two months doing them anyway, and you pay for the privilege.

sections.h2: The first thirty days: profile, then reviews, then everything else
body: For a local Chandigarh business, the Google Business Profile is not a marketing asset sitting alongside your website. In the map pack it *is* your website — it's what decides whether you appear at all, and it answers most of the searcher's questions before they ever click through.
The sequence we run, in order, and it rarely changes:
numbered: **Claim and complete the profile.** Primary category chosen deliberately — that single field does more ranking work than anything else on the profile — plus accurate secondary categories, precise hours, a services list, and real photos of the premises rather than stock.

**Fix name, address and phone consistency** everywhere it appears: Justdial, Sulekha, IndiaMART, Practo, association directories, your own footer. Inconsistent addresses are the most common reason a legitimate business under-ranks locally.

**Build a review flow, not a review campaign.** A QR code at the counter, a WhatsApp follow-up after service, a named person responsible. Thirty reviews arriving over three months reads as a business; thirty arriving on a Tuesday reads as something else.
**Answer every review**, including the bad ones, in a human voice. Response rate is visible to every future customer and converts better than the rating does.
**Then the website.** Speed, a page per service, a page per location, and content that answers what people actually ask at the front desk.

callout.title: On buying reviews
callout.body: Don't. Google removes them in waves, the removal takes your legitimate reviews' credibility with it, and in a city this small your competitors will notice a rating that jumped forty places in a fortnight. There's no published review threshold to hit — the honest target is simply beating the top three in your category, which in Chandigarh is usually a number you can reach in a quarter. See [review management](/services/review-management-services).

sections.h2: Three cities, two states, one union territory
body: The tricity is a single economy and three separate places as far as Google is concerned. Chandigarh is a union territory, Mohali sits in Punjab, Panchkula in Haryana, and the belt keeps spreading through Zirakpur, Kharar and New Chandigarh at Mullanpur.

Proximity dominates local ranking, so a clinic in Sector 34 will simply not show for a search made in Panchkula, no matter how good its site is. That leaves two honest options, and picking the wrong one wastes a year.

The other thing that makes this city unusual: sector addressing is how people genuinely think and search. Chandigarh's grid means "dentist sector 35", "gym sector 22", "showroom industrial area phase 1" are real queries with real intent. Mohali's phases and sectors work the same way, as do Panchkula's. Most Indian cities don't give you that clean a geographic vocabulary — use it.

sections.h2: Healthcare: PGI's gravity, and the clinics around it
body: PGIMER in Sector 12 makes Chandigarh the medical referral point for Punjab, Haryana and Himachal, and the private layer around it — Mohali's hospital corridor, Panchkula's clinics, specialist practices across the sectors — draws patients who travelled here specifically for treatment.

That produces search behaviour worth understanding. Fertility, orthopaedic, dental and cosmetic queries here often come from outside the tricity entirely — someone in Ludhiana or Hamirpur planning a trip. They ask different questions than a walk-in: cost, how many days they'll need to stay, whether consultation and procedure can happen in one visit, who exactly will treat them.

So the pages that convert aren't service pages. They're cost pages, protocol pages, and doctor pages with real credentials and registration numbers — what a patient making a five-hour trip actually needs, and what Google's quality guidelines hold health content to.

Two constraints to write inside from the start. Indian advertising law restricts claims about treating specific conditions, and pre-conception and pre-natal diagnostic law places hard limits on anything touching sex determination — which is directly relevant to fertility clinics. Neither rule prevents good content. Both punish lazy copy. The deeper version is on our [IVF clinics page](/seo-for/ivf-clinics).

sections.h2: Property, and the buyer in Brampton
body: Mohali's sectors and Aerocity, New Chandigarh at Mullanpur, Zirakpur and the Panchkula extension generate steady property demand, and an unusually large slice of it comes from outside India. Punjab's diaspora in Canada, the UK, the US and Australia buys here, and buys remotely.

That changes the work in ways local builders routinely miss. The buyer researches when your sales office is shut. They can't visit, so video walkthroughs and dated construction-progress pages do the job a site visit would. And they ask things a resident never would: is the title clear, what RERA registration does the project hold, how does repatriation of sale proceeds work, what NRI home-loan documents are needed, who manages the flat while they're away.

Content answering those questions ranks easily, because almost nobody writes it. 99acres and MagicBricks own the generic locality queries and always will, but they don't answer the NRI process questions — and those come from buyers further along than a portal browser.
And keep a page for the project name itself. You will outrank the portals for your own project with very little effort, which converts a paid portal lead into a free direct one.

We price SEO from **₹75,000/mo**, with smaller sites from **₹40,000/mo**, ex-GST. In most cities the ₹40,000 tier is for genuinely small sites. In Chandigarh it's the right answer more often, and we'd rather say so than upsell.

The ₹40,000 tier fits a single-location tricity business in a category with a handful of real competitors: a clinic, a salon, a coaching centre, a specialist retailer. The work is Business Profile, reviews, site speed, a page per service, a page per sector cluster you serve, and a modest content cadence. Against two to eight real rivals, that's usually enough.

You need the ₹75,000 tier when one of three things is true: you're competing beyond the tricity for regional or national queries; you have multiple branches, each needing its own profile, page and review flow; or you're in a category — property, healthcare, education — where the top of the market is already publishing seriously.

Either way the guarantee is identical. We freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search on day one, definition agreed in writing, and if we haven't beaten it in 90 days we keep working free until we do. We never promise a ranking position, because nobody controls Google's index. Three new clients a month across all cities is what makes a promise like that survivable. If you're deciding how wide to aim, start with [local SEO vs national SEO](/compare/local-seo-vs-national-seo).

faqs.q: Is SEO in Chandigarh easier than in Delhi or Bangalore?
faqs.a: In most local categories, yes — the field is genuinely smaller. Search your main service and count how many of the top ten are real local businesses with serious sites rather than directories. In Chandigarh that number is often between two and eight. That's the whole advantage, and it disappears if you compete nationally.

faqs.q: How many Google reviews do I need to rank in the Chandigarh map pack?
faqs.a: Google publishes no threshold, and anyone quoting one is guessing. The practical target is beating the review count and rating of the current top three in your category and area — in this city that's usually reachable within a quarter of steady, genuine collection. Bought reviews get removed in waves and cost you more than they gain.

faqs.q: Can one website rank across Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula?
faqs.a: One website, yes. One Business Profile, usually not. Proximity drives local ranking, so a Sector 34 address won't show for a Panchkula search. If customers come to you, you need a verified profile and a genuine landing page per branch. If you travel to them, a single profile with a tricity service area is correct.

faqs.q: Do you work with IVF and specialist clinics in Chandigarh and Mohali?
faqs.a: Yes. The content that converts is cost transparency, treatment protocols, travel and stay logistics, and doctor pages with real credentials and registration numbers — because many patients are travelling in from Punjab and Himachal. It has to be written inside India's advertising and pre-natal diagnostic rules, which constrain claims but not usefulness.

faqs.q: What does an SEO company in Chandigarh cost?
faqs.a: Ours starts at ₹40,000/mo for smaller single-location sites and ₹75,000/mo standard, ex-GST. In Chandigarh the ₹40,000 tier is the right fit more often than in bigger metros, because the competitive field is smaller. Multi-branch, regional or national targets push you to the higher tier.

faqs.q: Should I hire an agency before or after fixing my Google Business Profile?
faqs.a: Fix the profile first if you can. Claiming it, choosing the right primary category, correcting hours, adding real photos and starting a review flow costs nothing but attention, and it's the single largest local ranking lever. A retainer that begins before that work is done just bills you for it.
